messages:
sam_sales: Oakridge POC is blocked. Rerank calls fail with an embedding length error and they also see 429s when sending >16 candidates. Exec review tomorrow — need a quick remediation plan.

tia_se: do we have their exact embed model id + a sample request? is this via our python SDK or direct HTTP?

sam_sales: they sent this snippet from their engineer: `model: "oak-embed-768"` then they build a rerank payload with 20 candidate vectors and POST to `/v1/rerank`. Error in their UI: "unprocessable entity". They pasted the payload shape (list of 768-length floats x 20).

ryan_ml: most likely cause is vector length mismatch — the reranker configured for `ri-rerank-1536` expects 1536-d vectors. We should confirm with `GET /v1/models` on their account so they can see available encoder ids.

infra_bot: [service-log] service=reranker instance=rerank-canary-2 status=400 msg="embedding dimension mismatch expected=1536 got=768" code=EMB_DIM_MISMATCH

sam_sales: that matches. But what about the 429s? their usage is tiny, shouldn't hit org-wide limits.

tia_se: two possibilities: trial org has per-request compute/cost caps and a per-minute rate cap. Sending 20 dense vectors into one synchronous rerank increases CPU and memory; autoscaler might throttle or we may return 429 to protect SLOs. Ask them to try batching/chunking fewer candidates per request (8-12) and/or lower concurrency.

ryan_ml: short-term options: 1) point them to an existing compatible rerank model `ri-rerank-compat-768` if available; 2) provide a lightweight conversion shim (pad to 1536 with zeros + re-normalize) — tradeoff: semantic drift; 3) chunk candidates into multiple smaller rerank calls and aggregate.

sam_sales: sent them a quick chunking example. They also asked if the 768 vectors could be malformed (e.g., base64) — they're sending JSON arrays via Python requests.

ryan_ml: malformed encoding is unlikely if it's JSON arrays. Still ask them to paste one raw request body. Meanwhile here's a sample python pad snippet to try:`

```python
# naive pad 768->1536
import numpy as np
def pad_vector(v):
    v = np.array(v, dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] == 1536:
        return v.tolist()
    if v.shape[0] == 768:
        pad = np.zeros(1536 - 768, dtype=float)
        out = np.concatenate([v, pad])
        return out.tolist()
    raise ValueError('unexpected dim')
```

try that, but warn them about potential ranking changes. Also include curl example to validate model list: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models`.

infra_bot: [metric] rerank-canary-2 autoscale=1 pods cpu=85% mem=72% recent_429=5 window=2m

harry_am: from a pricing/ops angle, sustained high per-request compute is a Dedicated use-case. If Oakridge needs predictable throughput for ranking lots of candidates per query, we should quote reserved capacity. I'll prepare a short SOW estimate once we know target qps and avg candidates/query.

tia_se: immediate plan: 1) ask Oakridge to run `GET /v1/models` and share encoder id; 2) try chunking to 10 candidates per call and report if 429s persist; 3) try `ri-rerank-compat-768` if present, else run the pad shim; 4) we (eng) will add a preflight dim-check in SDK to fail early with clear guidance.

sam_sales: customer tried chunk_size=10 and no 429s — ranks returned. They then tried the pad shim; ranks changed but pipeline is functional. They want auto-conversion tooling in the SDK and a clear doc example.

ryan_ml: I'll add a minimal SDK lint that throws EMB_DIM_MISMATCH before sending and provide a convertor util and a docs snippet. I'll open a PR (ETA ~2h). tia_se: can you confirm we have `ri-rerank-compat-768` in model catalog for hosted customers? If so, add to the suggested fixes.

tia_se: will confirm. tagging follow-ups: @ryan_ml implement lint + example, @harry_am prepare Dedicated estimate if they need sustained throughput, @sam_sales keep the customer updated.

sam_sales: great — thanks team. I'll schedule a brief demo with Oakridge tomorrow to show chunking + pad shim and discuss next steps. :white_check_mark:

ryan_ml: noted. I'll also add a short note to the docs about quality implications when upcasting embeddings.

sam_sales: closing loop here — will post customer feedback in this thread after the demo. :rocket:
